analysis.title: Hyperscalers Burn $31 Billion In Q3 As Goldman Warns The AI Earnings Boom Has Stopped Accelerating
key_insights: Goldman's Ben Snider (US Weekly Kickstart, Q3 2026 midseason earnings update) says Q3 earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating. S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth is tracking at 33% y/y with 60% of the index reported, matching Q2 and against a 10-year median of 10%.
Index-level EPS growth was flat from Q2 to Q3 after the sharp Q1 and Q2 acceleration. The median stock slowed to 12% from 14%.

Beat quality is thinning. 60% of companies beat consensus by more than one standard deviation of estimates, above the 50% historical average but below the 64% average of the past four quarters. The aggregate upside surprise is well below Q1 and Q2.

Goldman expects S&P EPS growth, excluding non-recurring items, to slow from nearly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027. Median margins hit a record 16%, but analysts are trimming forward margins alongside rising energy prices.

Info Tech and Communication Services accounted for more than 60% of S&P Q3 EPS growth. Energy (EPS up 138%) added about another 20%. AI capex is contributing about half of S&P 500 EPS growth, an impulse expected to diminish as capex growth slows and depreciation builds.

Market breadth is widening through a 'catch up' and 'catch down'. Since the start of Q3 earnings season, 70% of S&P 500 companies posted positive returns but they account for only 50% of market cap. The S&P 500 is down 3% while the S&P 500 ex-AI is up 5%.

Reaction to beats differs by sector. The median beat earned 152bp of next-day outperformance versus a 95bp historical median. Industrials beats earned 371bp, Consumer Discretionary 326bp and Materials 204bp, while Communication Services beats were punished by 419bp. Non-TMT was +172bp and TMT -76bp.
Cyclicals, which saw large declines in hedge fund positioning, performed best. Hedge funds are the most bearish in five years. ServiceNow lost 34% in the week.

Hyperscaler capex outlook was stable this season. Analysts still expect roughly $800B of capex in 2026 and $1.2T for 2027, only slightly above the pre-earnings estimate. Goldman says capex growth and upside surprises to consensus are peaking, though spending will still rise substantially in 2027.

Consensus 2027 hyperscaler capex was $929B at the start of Q3 season and $1,105B at the start of Q4 season. It is now $1,163B. That is +$176B in one quarter versus +$58B this quarter. Growth falls from +96% this year to +44% in 2027 and +11% in 2028.
Goldman's Delta One head Rich Privorotsky said the point at which hyperscalers shift from needing capacity at almost any cost to optimizing returns on what they have built is the one to worry about.
AI infrastructure complex earnings growth (semis, power and others) is running at 80% y/y in Q3, more than 5x the 15% growth for the rest of the S&P. Consensus has it slowing to 40% by late 2027.

Hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT, ORCL) collectively reported negative free cash flow of $31B in Q3 2026, against about $60B a quarter through most of 2024. Capex now exceeds operating cash flow. Analysts expect group FCF to decline further in 2027 before turning positive in 2028.

Company FCF detail: Amazon burned $33.5B of free cash flow as capex reached $77.3B. Alphabet's FCF was negative for a second straight quarter. Meta authorized up to $97.5B for shareholders. Microsoft launched a $25B 10-part bond deal, its first since 2017.
The article's reading of Exhibit 17 puts group FCF at roughly $200B in 2025 (the extracted text is garbled), about $40B this year and about -$150B in 2027, before a rebound in 2028.

S&P put Meta's AA- rating on negative outlook, citing significant uncertainty around capex and free cash flow. Per the article, S&P sees Meta free operating cash flow deficits of $39B in 2026 and $71B in 2027, with FOCF possibly negative beyond 2028.

Credit stress signals: FT reported Blackstone expects Anthropic to land a high-junk rating after its IPO instead of investment grade. Goldman's credit desk finds AI default risk has nearly tripled since January.

Cloud revenue growth at Amazon, Google and Microsoft accelerated to 54% y/y in Q3 from 24% in early 2025, with backlogs approaching $2T. Snider calls this increasing signs of return on AI investments. Backlog growth decelerated slightly versus Q2, and expectations were raised by concentrated hedge fund positioning in the hyperscalers.

AI disruption risk is back in focus. Goldman analysts flagged disappointing Alphabet search revenues and reduced search referral traffic to Reddit, and Goldman economists note early signs of AI-related labor market disruption. Reddit fell 26% on Friday on a weak Q4 outlook.
Consensus 2027 EPS is up 2% since earnings season began, but revision breadth has moderated and is positive in only half of S&P sectors.
Goldman's S&P 500 targets are unchanged at 8,000 at year-end (about 5.5% above Friday's close) and 8,700 in 12 months, on 2027 EPS of $415 versus bottom-up consensus of $425.

Snider says energy prices and interest rates will determine whether non-tech parts of the market can keep rising. Friday: Brent settled at $116 (the article also cites $113 earlier), Dallas Fed's Logan said at least two more 25bp hikes are needed, and the US is reportedly preparing post-midterm strikes on Iran.

Friday market moves: Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% to 28,385 and briefly entered correction territory, the S&P fell 1.8% to 7,579, and Intel had its worst day in at least four decades. For October, Nasdaq is down about 6.6% and the S&P about 1%.
Next week brings 143 S&P companies (21% of market cap) reporting, plus the midterms, payrolls and the Treasury refunding.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue growth accelerated to 54% y/y with backlogs near $2T, which Snider reads as increasing signs of return on AI investments. Consensus still has 2027 capex rising to $1.2T and group FCF turning positive in 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Group FCF turned negative at -$31B in Q3, capex growth and upside surprises are peaking, and S&P sees Meta FOCF possibly negative beyond 2028. AI infrastructure earnings growth is expected to halve to 40% by late 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 2028 free cash flow rebound failing to arrive on schedule, or further rating agency actions on hyperscalers.

tension_points.bull_case: Breadth is broadening: the S&P ex-AI is up 5% while 70% of S&P companies posted positive returns since the start of earnings season, and cyclical beats are rewarded.
tension_points.bear_case: The catch-up leg depends on oil and rates cooperating, and Brent at $116 with Fed hikes still expected threatens it. The index is held back by TMT concentration.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy prices and interest rates rising further, with Logan calling for at least two more 25bp hikes and Brent at $116.
